title: Introduction
content:
1. Introduction to the Backup and Disaster Recovery System Backup and Disaster Recovery (DR) is a solution designed to protect application data and maintain service availability when unexpected incidents occur. By implementing backup and recovery mechanisms on AWS, businesses can reduce the risk of data loss and restore essential services when failures happen.
Amazon EC2 and Amazon RDS provide the main application and database infrastructure for the Maiora Fashion Store website. Amazon EC2 hosts the PHP-based web application, while Amazon RDS for MySQL stores customer accounts, product information, shopping carts, and order data.
Amazon S3 is used to store product images and other website assets. S3 Versioning helps preserve multiple versions of objects, while Cross-Region Replication (CRR) replicates objects from the primary bucket in Singapore to a destination bucket in Sydney.
AWS Backup provides centralized backup management for supported AWS resources, including Amazon EC2 and Amazon RDS. Backup plans, backup vaults, and recovery points help organize backup operations and support resource restoration when necessary.
2. Workshop Overview In this workshop, you will build and explore a Backup and Disaster Recovery solution for the Maiora Fashion Store website using AWS services across the Singapore and Sydney Regions.
“Application Infrastructure” uses Amazon VPC to provide the network environment for the website. An Amazon EC2 instance is deployed in a public subnet to host the PHP application, while Amazon RDS for MySQL is placed in a private network environment to store application data securely.
“Database and Storage Configuration” uses Amazon RDS for MySQL to manage the website database and Amazon S3 to store product images. S3 Versioning is enabled to preserve object versions, and Cross-Region Replication is configured to replicate objects to a bucket in the Sydney Region.
“Backup Management” uses AWS Backup to create and manage backup plans, backup vaults, and recovery points for Amazon EC2 and Amazon RDS. These backups provide recovery options when application or database resources are damaged or lost.
“Disaster Recovery and Restoration” focuses on restoring AWS resources from available recovery points and verifying the operation of the website after restoration. The workshop also examines the role of S3 object replication in protecting product images across Regions.
Through this workshop, you will practice deploying application infrastructure on AWS, configuring database and object storage, implementing backup mechanisms, setting up cross-region data replication, and performing restoration procedures to improve the data protection and recoverability of the Maiora Fashion Store website.

title: Proposal
content:
DESIGN AND IMPLEMENTATION OF A BACKUP AND DISASTER RECOVERY SYSTEM ON AMAZON WEB SERVICES (AWS) 1. Project Overview This project focuses on designing and implementing a Backup and Disaster Recovery (DR) system on the Amazon Web Services (AWS) platform for the Maiora Fashion Store e-commerce website.
The system uses AWS services such as Amazon EC2, Amazon RDS, Amazon S3, and AWS Backup to protect application servers, databases, and product image data. In addition, Amazon S3 Cross-Region Replication is used to replicate product image data from the Singapore Region to the Sydney Region, enhancing data protection in the event of an incident affecting the primary Region.
Through system deployment and recovery testing, the project evaluates the system’s recovery capabilities and proposes improvements to enhance availability, data security, and website continuity.
2. Problem Statement In an e-commerce environment, product information, customer details, order records, and product images play an important role in business operations. Data loss or server interruptions can prevent a website from operating normally, affecting user experience and order management activities.
Potential incidents include:
Amazon EC2 instance failures or accidental deletion. Amazon RDS database data loss or connectivity failures. Product images being deleted or overwritten in Amazon S3. Incidents in the primary Region that interrupt access to resources. Incorrect changes to application or database configurations. Without an appropriate backup and recovery mechanism, system restoration may take a significant amount of time, and important data may be lost.
Therefore, implementing a Backup and Disaster Recovery system on AWS is necessary to protect data, support resource restoration, and minimize the impact of unexpected incidents.
3. Proposed Solution Architecture 3.1. Architecture Model The system is deployed across two AWS Regions:
Primary Region: Asia Pacific (Singapore) - ap-southeast-1. Secondary Region: Asia Pacific (Sydney) - ap-southeast-2. In the Singapore Region, the Maiora Fashion Store website is deployed on Amazon EC2, Amazon RDS for MySQL is used to store application data, and Amazon S3 is used to store product images.
AWS Backup is used to create and manage recovery points for EC2 and RDS resources. For product image data, Amazon S3 Versioning combined with Cross-Region Replication helps retain different object versions and replicate data to the Sydney Region.
3.2. Main Components Amazon VPC: Provides an isolated network environment for the system, including Public Subnets and Private Subnets. Amazon EC2: Hosts the application server running Amazon Linux, Apache, and PHP. Amazon RDS for MySQL: Stores the shop database, including user, product, shopping cart, and order information. Amazon S3: Stores product images used by the website. Amazon S3 Versioning: Retains multiple versions of objects to support recovery when data is overwritten or deleted. Amazon S3 Cross-Region Replication: Replicates eligible product image objects from the Singapore bucket to the Sydney bucket according to the configured replication rules. AWS Backup: Manages backup plans, Backup Vaults, and Recovery Points for supported resources. Amazon CloudWatch: Supports resource monitoring and activity tracking when configured. 3.3. Operating Principles Users access the website through the Amazon EC2 application server. The EC2 instance connects to Amazon RDS for MySQL to retrieve and update application data. Product images are stored in Amazon S3 and accessed by the website through object URLs.
AWS Backup protects selected resources and creates Recovery Points for restoration purposes. When an incident occurs, administrators can select an appropriate Recovery Point to restore EC2 or RDS resources.
For product image data, S3 Versioning allows previous object versions to be retrieved. Cross-Region Replication supports the replication of eligible objects to the Sydney bucket.
Resource restoration and service switching are performed manually by administrators within the scope of this implementation.
3.4. Architecture Diagram 4. Technical Implementation Scope The project focuses on the following implementation activities:
4.1. Network Infrastructure Design and Configuration Create an Amazon VPC with the CIDR block 10.0.0.0/16. Divide the network into Public Subnets and Private Subnets. Configure the Internet Gateway and Route Tables. Configure Security Groups to control network traffic. Deploy EC2 in a Public Subnet and configure connectivity to RDS in a Private Subnet. 4.2. Application Server Deployment Launch an EC2 instance running Amazon Linux. Install and configure Apache and PHP. Deploy the Maiora Fashion Store e-commerce website. Verify website accessibility and the operation of its main functions. 4.3. Database and Storage Configuration Create an Amazon RDS for MySQL instance. Initialize the shop database. Configure connectivity from EC2 to RDS through Security Groups. Create an Amazon S3 bucket to store product images. Enable S3 Versioning to protect different versions of stored objects. Configure Cross-Region Replication from Singapore to Sydney. 4.4. Backup System Implementation Create an AWS Backup Vault. Configure a Backup Plan and Backup Rules. Select EC2 and RDS resources for backup. Execute Backup Jobs. Verify backup job statuses and generated Recovery Points. 4.5. Disaster Recovery and Restoration Testing Restore the EC2 instance from a Recovery Point. Restore the RDS database from a backup. Verify application-to-database connectivity after restoration. Test website accessibility. Test product image recovery using S3 Versioning. Verify replicated data in the Sydney Region. 4.6. System Testing and Evaluation Verify website functionality after deployment. Simulate application server failure scenarios. Simulate accidental data deletion or modification. Perform resource restoration using Recovery Points. Evaluate restoration results and identify limitations of the implemented model. 5. Implementation Roadmap and Milestones Phase Activities Expected Results Phase 1 Study AWS and Backup and Disaster Recovery services Identify the technologies to be used Phase 2 Design the architecture and configure VPC Complete the network infrastructure Phase 3 Deploy EC2 and the website Website becomes operational Phase 4 Configure RDS and S3 Complete the data storage environment Phase 5 Configure AWS Backup and S3 Replication Establish data protection mechanisms Phase 6 Perform restoration and testing Evaluate recovery capabilities Phase 7 Consolidate results and complete the report Complete the project 6. Estimated Budget The AWS services used in this project may incur costs depending on resource runtime, storage capacity, the number of backups, and data transfer volume.
The main components that may generate costs include:
Amazon EC2: Costs for the compute instance and EBS storage. Amazon RDS: Costs for the DB instance, storage capacity, and backups. Amazon S3: Costs for object storage, Versioning, and access requests. AWS Backup: Costs for backup storage and related operations. Cross-Region Replication: Costs for replication requests and data transfer between Regions. Network services: Potential charges for data transfer and network resources. To control the budget, the system is deployed within a testing environment. Unnecessary resources will be stopped or deleted after testing is completed. Backups and data required for evaluation will be retained according to the project requirements.
7. Risk Assessment and Mitigation Risk Impact Mitigation EC2 instance failure or accidental deletion Website becomes unavailable Restore EC2 from AWS Backup RDS becomes inaccessible Website cannot retrieve database records Restore RDS from a Recovery Point and update the endpoint if necessary Product images are deleted Product images become unavailable on the website Use S3 Versioning or replicated data Data is overwritten Stored content becomes incorrect Retrieve a previous object version Primary Region failure Resources in the primary Region become inaccessible Use replicated data in the Sydney Region and perform the appropriate recovery procedures Incorrect IAM configuration Backup or Restore operations fail Verify IAM Roles, Trust Relationships, and required permissions The current implementation does not provide automatic failover of the entire system to the Sydney Region. EC2 and RDS restoration, as well as application configuration updates, are performed manually. This limitation must be considered when evaluating the proposed solution.
8. Expected Outcomes Upon completion, the project is expected to achieve the following results:
Build an AWS infrastructure environment for the Maiora Fashion Store website. Successfully deploy the website using EC2, RDS for MySQL, and S3. Establish backup mechanisms for EC2 and RDS using AWS Backup. Create and manage Recovery Points for resource restoration. Configure S3 Versioning and Cross-Region Replication to improve product image data protection. Perform application server and database restoration from backups. Test selected data loss and service interruption scenarios. Evaluate the advantages, limitations, and future development directions of the AWS Backup and Disaster Recovery model. Through this project, the implementation applies knowledge of cloud computing, infrastructure management, data storage, backup, and system recovery to a practical application environment.

title: Prerequisites
content:
1. Overview of the Deployment Environment To deploy a Backup and Disaster Recovery system for the Maiora Fashion Store website, we need to prepare the AWS cloud environment, application infrastructure, database, and storage resources.
The primary environment is deployed in the Singapore Region (ap-southeast-1), where the website runs on an Amazon EC2 instance and uses Amazon RDS for MySQL to store application data. Amazon S3 is used to store product images and website assets.
The Sydney Region (ap-southeast-2) is used as the destination for Amazon S3 Cross-Region Replication. This configuration helps maintain copies of product images in another AWS Region. AWS Backup is used to manage backup and recovery points for supported resources, including Amazon EC2 and Amazon RDS.
2. Required Components Amazon Web Services (AWS): Provides the cloud infrastructure and services required to deploy the application, store data, and implement backup and recovery mechanisms.
Amazon VPC: Provides an isolated network environment for deploying application and database resources. The VPC includes public and private subnets, route tables, an Internet Gateway, and security groups.
Amazon EC2: Hosts the Maiora Fashion Store website using PHP and Apache. The EC2 instance acts as the application server and communicates with the database hosted on Amazon RDS.
Amazon RDS for MySQL: Provides a managed relational database service for storing website information, including customer accounts, product details, shopping carts, and orders.
Amazon S3: Stores product images and website assets. S3 Versioning is used to preserve object versions, while Cross-Region Replication (CRR) replicates objects from the primary bucket in Singapore to a destination bucket in Sydney.
AWS Backup: Provides centralized backup management for supported AWS resources, including Amazon EC2 and Amazon RDS. Backup vaults and recovery points are used to organize and restore protected resources.
Administration Computer: Used to access the AWS Management Console, configure AWS resources, connect to the EC2 instance, manage application files, and verify the website.

A destination S3 bucket in the Sydney Region (ap-southeast-2) is prepared for Cross-Region Replication. AWS Backup permissions and the required backup configuration are available for protecting Amazon EC2 and Amazon RDS resources. The website application files and database configuration are ready for deployment and verification. An administration computer with an Internet connection and a modern web browser is available to manage AWS resources. The destination S3 bucket in the Sydney Region and the necessary AWS Backup configuration will provide the foundation for implementing cross-region object replication and resource backup.
These preparations enable us to proceed with application deployment, database and storage configuration, backup management, and restoration procedures in the following sections.

Report on the Mini Meetup – API Standards in Backend Development 1. Event Objectives The Mini Meetup – First Cloud AI Journey, held on August 22, 2026, was a knowledge-sharing event organized by the FCAJ community. The event focused on API standards in Backend development, helping participants understand how APIs support communication and data exchange between different components of modern software systems.
The main objectives of the event were:
To understand the role of APIs in connecting applications and exchanging data between system components. To explore important standards and principles for designing Backend APIs. To understand the importance of building APIs that are consistent, secure, maintainable, and scalable. To encourage continuous learning and knowledge sharing within the technology community. 2. Speaker and Topic Nguyen Nhan – FCAJ Member: API Standards in Backend Development. 3. Key Topics 3.1. Overview of APIs in Backend Development An API (Application Programming Interface) provides an interface that allows applications or software components to communicate and exchange data. In modern software systems, APIs are commonly used to connect Frontend applications with Backend services, integrate different services, and support communication between systems.
Key concepts included:
Understanding the concept of APIs and their role in software architecture. Recognizing how APIs enable communication between applications and services. Understanding the importance of designing APIs with clear and consistent structures. Recognizing how APIs support integration between components in larger systems. This session helped me understand that APIs are an important part of Backend development and provide a structured way for different software components to interact.
3.2. API Design Standards and Principles The presentation focused on important standards and principles for designing Backend APIs, emphasizing usability, maintainability, and scalability as systems develop.
Key aspects included:
Consistency: Maintaining consistent endpoint naming conventions, data structures, and response formats. Usability: Designing clear endpoints that other applications and services can easily understand and integrate with. Maintainability: Organizing APIs logically to simplify updates, troubleshooting, and the development of new features. Scalability: Designing APIs with a structure that can accommodate future system growth. Compatibility: Minimizing breaking changes that could affect applications already using the APIs. These principles demonstrate that API development involves more than processing requests. It also requires careful design to ensure that services remain reliable and easy to maintain over time.
3.3. The Role of APIs in Modern Systems As software systems become more complex, APIs play an increasingly important role in enabling different services to communicate and work together. Well-designed APIs can reduce dependencies between components, support integration, and make future system development easier.
Important considerations when designing APIs include:
Clearly defining the purpose of each endpoint and the data it exchanges. Standardizing request handling, response structures, and error messages. Prioritizing authentication, authorization, and data protection. Considering API versioning when modifying existing functionality or introducing new features. Providing clear documentation to support development and integration. These principles provide a foundation for developing and maintaining software systems in practical environments.

API Design: Recognized the importance of consistency, usability, and maintainability when designing service interfaces. System Integration: Learned how APIs facilitate communication and data exchange between applications and services. API Security: Understood the importance of authentication, authorization, and data protection when exposing application interfaces. Scalability and Compatibility: Recognized the need to design APIs that can support system growth without unnecessarily affecting existing functionality. 4.2. Personal Development Skills Improved my ability to explore and understand new technical concepts. Recognized the value of sharing technical knowledge and practical experience within a technology community. Gained motivation to learn more about API design, documentation, and testing. Understood the importance of continuous learning in keeping up with modern software development. 5. Application to My Internship Project My internship project is titled “Research and Implementation of a Backup and Disaster Recovery System on Amazon Web Services (AWS).”
The project uses Maiora, a fashion e-commerce website, as a practical application to demonstrate cloud infrastructure deployment, data backup, and system recovery.

The knowledge can be applied in the following ways:
Backend Application Development: Apply API design principles when developing or extending Backend functions for the Maiora website, ensuring that interfaces are clear and maintainable. AWS Service Management: Explore how AWS provides APIs that allow cloud resources and services to be managed programmatically. System Integration: Understand how APIs can support communication between application components and external services. Security and Access Management: Pay attention to authentication, authorization, and data protection when applications communicate with services or access cloud resources. Future Automation: Explore the potential of APIs for automating cloud resource management and supporting backup and recovery operations in future development. These applications provide a broader understanding of the relationship between Backend development, cloud services, and infrastructure management.
6. Event Experience Participating in the Mini Meetup – First Cloud AI Journey on August 22, 2026, gave me an opportunity to explore API standards in Backend development and understand their importance in modern software architecture.
Through the presentation by Nguyen Nhan, I gained a better understanding of API design principles, particularly consistency, maintainability, compatibility, and scalability. These principles are important for enabling software components to communicate effectively and supporting the development of applications over time.
The session also helped me recognize that security and documentation are essential considerations when designing APIs. A well-structured interface should not only work correctly but also be understandable, secure, and convenient for future maintenance.
In addition to the technical content, the knowledge-sharing environment of the FCAJ community encouraged me to continue learning, exchanging experiences, and exploring technologies related to Backend development and AWS.
7. Conclusion and Lessons Learned Through the Mini Meetup – First Cloud AI Journey on August 22, 2026, I gained a better understanding of APIs and their role in connecting and integrating components within modern software systems.
The most important lesson was that API design should prioritize consistency, usability, security, maintainability, and scalability. These principles help ensure that applications and services can communicate effectively and remain easier to develop and maintain.
The knowledge gained provides a useful foundation for further developing the Maiora application, exploring AWS service management interfaces, and understanding how APIs can support future automation and integration in the Backup and Disaster Recovery environment.

title: AWS Architecture Design
content:
1. Overview of the System Architecture The system architecture is designed to deploy and protect the Maiora Fashion Store website using Amazon Web Services (AWS). The solution combines cloud infrastructure, database services, object storage, backup services, and cross-region data replication to improve data protection and system recoverability.
The primary environment is deployed in the Asia Pacific (Singapore) Region (ap-southeast-1). It hosts the website application, database, and primary storage resources.
The Asia Pacific (Sydney) Region (ap-southeast-2) is used as the destination for Amazon S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR), providing an additional copy of product images in another AWS Region.
The architecture consists of the following main components:
Amazon VPC: Provides an isolated network environment for application and database resources. Amazon EC2: Hosts the Maiora Fashion Store website using Apache and PHP. Amazon RDS for MySQL: Stores application data, including product information, customer accounts, shopping carts, and orders. Amazon S3: Stores product images and uses Versioning to maintain object versions. Amazon S3 Cross-Region Replication: Replicates objects from the primary S3 bucket in Singapore to a destination bucket in Sydney. AWS Backup: Manages backup and recovery points for supported resources, including EC2 and RDS. 2. Proposed System Architecture The system is divided into two main geographical environments:
2.1. Primary Region – Singapore The Singapore Region is the primary operating environment of Maiora Fashion Store.
Its main components include:
An Amazon VPC named backup-dr-vpc with the CIDR block 10.0.0.0/16. An EC2 application server named app-server, deployed in a public subnet. An Amazon RDS MySQL database named backup-dr-db, configured for private access. An Amazon S3 bucket named myproject-backup-primary-671657, used to store product images. An AWS Backup vault named BackupDR-Vault, used to manage backup recovery points. The EC2 instance runs the Apache web server and PHP application. It communicates with the RDS database through a private network connection.
The application retrieves product images from Amazon S3 instead of storing all image files directly on the EC2 instance.
2.2. Secondary Region – Sydney The Sydney Region provides an additional storage location for replicated product images.
Its main component is the destination Amazon S3 bucket, which receives replicated objects from the primary bucket in Singapore through Cross-Region Replication.
This arrangement provides another copy of product images in a separate AWS Region.
The Sydney Region is used as a secondary storage location in this workshop. It is not considered a fully deployed application recovery environment because separate EC2 and RDS application resources are not provisioned there.
3. Architecture Diagram The following diagram illustrates the relationship between the primary application environment, backup services, and secondary storage environment.
The main data flows are:
Users access the Maiora Fashion Store website through the Internet. The EC2 application server processes website requests and communicates with the RDS MySQL database. Product images are retrieved from the primary S3 bucket. Amazon S3 Cross-Region Replication copies eligible objects from Singapore to the destination bucket in Sydney. AWS Backup creates recovery points for supported resources, including the EC2 application server and RDS database. When a failure occurs, administrators can restore resources from available backup recovery points. 4. Data Protection and Backup Strategy The solution applies different protection mechanisms according to the type of data and AWS resource.
4.1. Application Server Backup The EC2 application server hosts the website source code and application runtime environment.
AWS Backup is used to create recovery points for the EC2 instance. When the application server becomes unavailable or its configuration is damaged, administrators can restore the instance from an available recovery point.
After restoration, the application configuration and network associations must be checked before the website is accessed again.
4.2. Database Backup Amazon RDS for MySQL stores important application data, including:
Product information. Customer account information. Shopping cart data. Order information. Order details. AWS Backup is used to protect the RDS database by creating recovery points according to the configured backup process.
When data is lost or the database becomes unavailable, administrators can restore the database from a suitable recovery point.
Because a restored RDS database may have a different endpoint, the application database configuration must be updated when necessary.
4.3. Product Image Protection Amazon S3 stores the product images used by the website.
The following mechanisms are applied:
S3 Versioning maintains multiple versions of objects. Cross-Region Replication copies eligible objects to a destination bucket in another AWS Region. Administrators can use available object versions to recover from accidental changes or deletions, subject to the configured versioning and replication behavior. Cross-Region Replication operates asynchronously. Therefore, replication should not be assumed to be instantaneous, and replication status should be checked when validating recovery.
5. System Recovery Scenarios The architecture supports several recovery scenarios.
Failure Scenario Recovery Approach EC2 application server failure Restore the EC2 instance from an AWS Backup recovery point. RDS database failure or data loss Restore the database from an available RDS recovery point. Product image modification or deletion Recover an appropriate object version from Amazon S3. Primary S3 storage disruption Use replicated objects in the Sydney destination bucket, subject to replication status and application configuration. Website unavailable after restoration Check application services, database endpoint, network settings, and public IP associations. The recovery process depends on the availability of backup recovery points, replicated objects, and the correct configuration of restored resources.
6. Security and Network Considerations The architecture separates application and database resources to reduce unnecessary exposure.
The main security considerations include:
The EC2 application server is deployed in a public subnet to provide website access. The RDS database is configured with public access disabled. The RDS Security Group allows MySQL traffic on TCP port 3306 only from the EC2 application server Security Group. SSH access to EC2 should be restricted to trusted administrator IP addresses. Amazon S3 Block Public Access and bucket policies should be configured according to the website’s image delivery requirements. AWS Backup permissions should follow the principle of least privilege. 7. Expected Results After completing the architecture design, the overall structure of the Maiora Fashion Store Backup and Disaster Recovery system is established.
The Singapore Region operates the website and database, while the Sydney Region stores replicated product images. AWS Backup provides recovery points for the EC2 application server and RDS database, and S3 Versioning provides additional protection for product images.
This architecture provides the foundation for the next workshop sections, where the AWS network, application, database, storage, backup, and recovery configurations will be implemented and tested.

Instead of relying entirely on theoretical documentation, the project combines different interactive learning methods to help learners acquire knowledge and visualize concepts related to cloud computing.

Building a platform that helps learners explore AWS knowledge visually. Creating an interactive learning environment through 3D models. Integrating simulated labs to support hands-on learning. title: Workshop
content:
Research and Implementation of a Backup and Disaster Recovery System on Amazon Web Services (AWS) Overview In this workshop, we will explore the design and implementation of a Backup and Disaster Recovery (DR) system on Amazon Web Services (AWS) for the Maiora Fashion Store website.
The system is deployed primarily in the Singapore Region (ap-southeast-1), where Amazon EC2 hosts the PHP-based website and Amazon RDS for MySQL stores application data, including customer accounts, product information, shopping carts, and orders. Amazon S3 is used to store product images and other website assets.
To improve data protection, Amazon S3 Versioning is enabled to preserve multiple versions of objects. Cross-Region Replication (CRR) is configured to replicate product images from the primary S3 bucket in Singapore to a destination bucket in the Sydney Region (ap-southeast-2).
In addition, AWS Backup is used as a centralized backup management service to protect supported resources, including Amazon EC2 and Amazon RDS. Backup vaults and recovery points provide the foundation for restoring application infrastructure and database resources when failures or data loss occur.
Through this workshop, we will practice preparing the AWS environment, deploying the application, configuring database and storage services, implementing backup mechanisms, and performing recovery tests to verify the integrity and availability of the website and its data.
The main topics include:
AWS Architecture Design: Design the backup and disaster recovery architecture for the Maiora Fashion Store website using AWS services. AWS Network Infrastructure: Create and configure Amazon VPC, public and private subnets, route tables, Internet Gateway, and Security Groups. Application Deployment on Amazon EC2: Deploy and configure the PHP-based Maiora Fashion Store website using Apache on an EC2 instance. Database Configuration: Configure Amazon RDS for MySQL and establish secure connectivity between the application server and the database. Amazon S3 Storage and Replication: Store product images, enable S3 Versioning, and configure Cross-Region Replication between Singapore and Sydney. Backup Management with AWS Backup: Create backup vaults and backup plans, protect EC2 and RDS resources, and manage recovery points. Disaster Recovery and Restoration: Perform restoration procedures for EC2 and RDS resources and verify the recovered application and database. System Testing and Resource Cleanup: Test backup and recovery operations, verify website functionality and data integrity, and clean up AWS resources when necessary. Contents Workshop Overview Prerequisites Architecture Design AWS Network Infrastructure Deployment Maiora Fashion Store Deployment on Amazon EC2 Amazon RDS Database Configuration Amazon S3 Storage and Cross-Region Replication AWS Backup Configuration and Management Disaster Recovery and Restoration Testing System Verification and AWS Resource Cleanup

title: Network and Application Setup
content:
1. Overview In this section, we will configure the AWS network infrastructure and deploy the application server for the Maiora Fashion Store system.
The primary infrastructure is deployed in the Singapore Region (ap-southeast-1). The VPC provides network isolation, while the EC2 instance hosts the PHP-based web application.
The main tasks include:
Creating and configuring an Amazon VPC. Creating public and private subnets. Configuring an Internet Gateway and route tables. Creating security groups for the application server. Launching an EC2 instance. Installing and configuring the web server environment. Deploying and verifying the Maiora Fashion Store website. 2. Create an Amazon VPC Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC) allows us to create an isolated virtual network in AWS.
In this workshop, we create a VPC named backup-dr-vpc in the Singapore Region.
2.1. VPC configuration Use the following configuration:
Parameter Value Name backup-dr-vpc Region Asia Pacific (Singapore) IPv4 CIDR 10.0.0.0/16 Availability Zones 2 Public Subnets 2 Private Subnets 2 NAT Gateway Not configured VPC Endpoints Not configured 2.2. Create the VPC Open the AWS Management Console. Navigate to VPC. Select Your VPCs. Click Create VPC. Enter the VPC name and IPv4 CIDR block. Create the VPC. 3. Configure Subnets Subnets divide the VPC network into smaller network segments.
The workshop uses public subnets for the application server and private subnets for internal resources such as the database.
3.1. Public subnets Public subnets are associated with a route table that directs internet-bound traffic through the Internet Gateway.
The EC2 application server is deployed in a public subnet to allow users to access the website.
3.2. Private subnets Private subnets are intended for resources that should not be directly accessible from the public internet.
The Amazon RDS MySQL database is deployed in private subnets.
4. Configure Internet Gateway and Route Tables 4.1. Create an Internet Gateway An Internet Gateway enables communication between resources in public subnets and the internet.
Steps:
Open the VPC console. Select Internet Gateways. Click Create internet gateway. Enter a name, such as backup-dr-igw. Attach the Internet Gateway to backup-dr-vpc. 4.2. Configure the public route table Configure the public route table with the following route:
Destination Target 10.0.0.0/16 local 0.0.0.0/0 Internet Gateway Associate this route table with the public subnets.
Private subnets do not receive a direct route to the Internet Gateway in this workshop.
5. Create Security Groups Security Groups act as virtual firewalls that control inbound and outbound traffic for AWS resources.
5.1. Application Security Group Create a security group named ec2-sg for the EC2 application server.
Configure the inbound rules as follows:
Type Protocol Port Source SSH TCP 22 Administrator’s IP address HTTP TCP 80 0.0.0.0/0 HTTPS TCP 443 0.0.0.0/0 SSH access should be restricted to trusted administrator IP addresses.
5.2. Database Security Group The RDS database uses a separate security group named rds-sg.
Configure the inbound rule:
Type Protocol Port Source MySQL/Aurora TCP 3306 EC2 application security group (ec2-sg) This configuration allows the application server to communicate with the database without exposing the database directly to the internet.
6. Launch the EC2 Application Server Amazon EC2 provides the virtual machine used to host the Maiora Fashion Store website.
6.1. EC2 instance configuration Use the following configuration as a reference:
Parameter Value Instance name app-server Region Singapore Instance type t3.micro Operating system Amazon Linux VPC backup-dr-vpc Subnet Public subnet Auto-assign public IP Enabled Security Group ec2-sg Select or create an appropriate key pair for SSH access.
6.2. Launch the instance Open the EC2 console. Select Instances. Click Launch instances. Enter app-server as the instance name. Select an Amazon Linux AMI. Choose the t3.micro instance type. Configure the VPC and public subnet. Attach the ec2-sg security group. Select the key pair. Launch the instance. 7. Configure the Web Server Environment After the EC2 instance is running, connect to it using SSH.
Install and start the Apache web server and PHP environment.
Example commands for Amazon Linux:
sudo dnf update -y sudo dnf install -y httpd php php-fpm php-mysqlnd sudo systemctl enable httpd sudo systemctl start httpd sudo systemctl enable php-fpm sudo systemctl start php-fpm Verify the Apache service:
sudo systemctl status httpd Verify the PHP version:
php -v The web server should be running before deploying the application files.
8. Deploy the Maiora Fashion Store Website The Maiora Fashion Store application is developed using PHP and MySQL.
The application files are deployed to the Apache document root:
/var/www/html The main application components include:
index.php: Homepage. products.php: Product listing. login.php: User login. register.php: User registration. cart.php: Shopping cart. checkout.php: Order checkout. orders.php: Order history. auth.php: Authentication and session handling. The database connection configuration is stored separately at:
/etc/shop/db-config.php This keeps database credentials outside the website’s public document root.
Ensure that the application files and configuration have appropriate ownership and permissions.
9. Verify the Application After deploying the application, access the website using the EC2 public IPv4 address or its associated Elastic IP.
Verify the following functions:
The homepage loads successfully. Product information is displayed. Product images are loaded from Amazon S3. Users can access the login and registration pages. The shopping cart interface is displayed. The website can access its configured database through the application. 10. Expected Results After completing this section, the following components should be available:
An Amazon VPC named backup-dr-vpc. Public and private subnets configured in the Singapore Region. An Internet Gateway and public route table. Security groups for the EC2 application server and RDS database. An EC2 instance named app-server. Apache and PHP installed and running. The Maiora Fashion Store website deployed and accessible. The infrastructure is now ready for the database and storage configuration described in the next section.

title: Database and Storage Configuration
content:
4.5. Database and Storage Configuration In this section, Amazon RDS and Amazon S3 are configured to provide database and object storage services for the Maiora Fashion Store application.
The database stores application information such as user accounts, product details, shopping carts, and customer orders. Amazon S3 is used to store product images separately from the EC2 application server.
4.5.1. Creating an Amazon RDS MySQL Instance Amazon RDS for MySQL is used as the relational database service for the application.
The database instance is configured with the following settings:
Database engine: MySQL. DB instance identifier: backup-dr-db. Instance class: db.t3.micro. Storage: 20 GB. Database name: shop. Public access: No. VPC: backup-dr-vpc. VPC security group: rds-sg. The RDS instance is deployed in the private network to prevent direct access from the public Internet.
4.5.2. Configuring Database Connectivity The RDS security group is configured to allow MySQL connections on TCP port 3306 only from the EC2 application server security group.
This configuration ensures that the database is accessible to the application server without exposing the database directly to the Internet.
The application uses a separate configuration file to store database connection settings. Sensitive information such as database passwords is not stored in the public source code repository.
4.5.3. Creating the Application Database After the database instance is available, the shop database is prepared for the Maiora Fashion Store application.
The database contains tables for managing the application’s main functions:
users: stores customer account information. products: stores product information. cart_items: stores shopping cart items. orders: stores customer order information. order_items: stores product details associated with each order. These tables support the main shopping functions, including account registration, login, product display, shopping cart management, and order processing.
4.5.4. Creating an Amazon S3 Bucket Amazon S3 is used to store product images separately from the EC2 application server.
A dedicated S3 bucket is created for the product images.
The bucket is configured with the following settings:
Bucket name: myproject-backup-primary-671657. AWS Region: Asia Pacific (Singapore). Object ownership: Bucket owner enforced. Block Public Access: configured according to the application’s image-access method. Server-side encryption: SSE-S3. The application retrieves product images from S3 using their object locations.

title: Backup and Cross-Region Replication
content:
4.6. Backup and Cross-Region Replication In this section, AWS Backup and Amazon S3 Cross-Region Replication are configured to protect the application infrastructure and product images of the Maiora Fashion Store.
AWS Backup is used to create and manage backups of EC2 and RDS resources in the primary AWS Region (Singapore). Amazon S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) is used to replicate product images from the Singapore bucket to a destination bucket in Sydney.
4.6.1. Creating an AWS Backup Vault AWS Backup Vault is used to organize and manage recovery points created by backup operations.
A backup vault named BackupDR-Vault is used in the Singapore Region to store recovery points for the application resources.
The vault provides a centralized location for managing backup data and supports the restoration process when resources need to be recovered.
4.6.2. Backing Up EC2 and RDS Resources AWS Backup is used to create backups of the EC2 application server and the RDS MySQL database.
The protected resources include:
EC2: the application server hosting the Maiora Fashion Store website. RDS: the MySQL database storing application data. On-demand backup jobs are initiated to create recovery points for the selected resources.
These recovery points provide backup data that can be used to restore the application server or database when necessary.
4.6.3. Monitoring Backup Jobs AWS Backup provides backup job information to track the progress and status of backup operations.
The backup job status is checked to verify whether the backup operation has completed successfully.
Important information includes:
Resource type and resource identifier. Backup job status. Backup start and completion time. Recovery point information. A completed backup job indicates that AWS Backup has successfully created the corresponding recovery point.
4.6.4. Enabling Amazon S3 Versioning Amazon S3 Versioning is enabled on the source bucket in Singapore.
Versioning maintains multiple versions of an object in the same bucket. When an existing object is overwritten or deleted, previous versions can be retained according to the bucket’s versioning behavior.
This feature helps protect product images from accidental overwrites or deletions and provides additional recovery options.
4.6.5. Configuring S3 Cross-Region Replication Amazon S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) is configured to replicate product images from the source bucket in Singapore to a destination bucket in Sydney.
The replication configuration includes:
Source bucket: myproject-backup-primary-671657. Source Region: Asia Pacific (Singapore). Destination Region: Asia Pacific (Sydney). Replication scope: product image objects under the products/ prefix. Replication role: an IAM role authorized to replicate objects between the two buckets. Both source and destination buckets must have S3 Versioning enabled.
After the replication rule is enabled, eligible new objects uploaded to the source bucket are automatically replicated to the destination bucket. Replication is asynchronous, so the destination object may not appear immediately.
4.6.6. Verifying Replicated Objects in Sydney After the replication rule is configured, the destination bucket in Sydney is checked to verify that product images have been replicated.
The destination bucket provides a secondary copy of eligible product image objects in another AWS Region.
This helps improve data availability if the source Region or source bucket becomes unavailable.
Note that S3 Cross-Region Replication does not automatically replicate every historical object uploaded before the replication rule was enabled. Existing objects may require S3 Batch Replication. Replication behavior for delete markers and permanent version deletions also depends on the replication configuration.
4.6.7. Section Summary In this section, AWS Backup and Amazon S3 Cross-Region Replication are configured to protect different parts of the Maiora Fashion Store system.
AWS Backup provides recovery points for the EC2 application server and RDS database, while S3 Cross-Region Replication provides a secondary copy of eligible product images in Sydney.
Together, these mechanisms improve the protection and recoverability of application infrastructure and stored image data. sted zone(/images/5-Workshop/5.6-Cleanup/delete-zone.png)

title: Disaster Recovery and Restoration
content:
4.7. Disaster Recovery and Restoration This section demonstrates the recovery process for the Maiora Fashion Store application when infrastructure or data becomes unavailable.
AWS Backup is used to restore the EC2 application server and the RDS MySQL database from available recovery points. Amazon S3 is also checked to verify that replicated product images remain available in the Sydney Region.
The recovery procedure focuses on restoring application components and verifying that the website can operate correctly after recovery.
4.7.1. Selecting an EC2 Recovery Point When the EC2 application server becomes unavailable or its data needs to be recovered, an available recovery point can be selected from AWS Backup.
The recovery point contains backup data of the EC2 instance at the time the backup was created.
The recovery point is selected based on its resource identifier, creation time, and backup status.
4.7.2. Restoring the EC2 Application Server The EC2 instance is restored through AWS Backup using the selected recovery point.
During the restore process, the required instance configuration and network settings are reviewed before completing the operation.
After the restore job completes, AWS creates the restored EC2 instance. The restored instance is checked in the EC2 console to verify that it is running.
4.7.3. Reassociating the Elastic IP Address If the original application server uses an Elastic IP address, the address may need to be associated with the restored EC2 instance.
The Elastic IP address is checked in the EC2 console and associated with the restored instance when necessary.
This step allows users to access the website through the same public IP address, provided that the address is available and belongs to the same AWS Region.
4.7.4. Restoring the RDS MySQL Database The RDS database is restored from an available AWS Backup recovery point or an existing database snapshot.
During the restore process, the database configuration is reviewed, including the DB instance identifier, VPC, subnet group, security group, and database accessibility settings.
AWS RDS creates a new DB instance for the restored database. The application connection configuration must be updated if the restored database has a different endpoint.
4.7.5. Verifying the Restored Database After the restored RDS instance becomes available, its status and connection configuration are reviewed.
The application database is checked to confirm that the expected data is available.
The database contains the main application tables:
users products cart_items orders order_items This verification helps confirm that the database recovery process has restored the required application data.
4.7.6. Verifying Product Images in the Sydney Region The destination S3 bucket in Sydney is checked to confirm that replicated product images remain available.
The objects under the products/ prefix are reviewed to verify that the expected images are present.
These replicated objects provide an additional copy of eligible product images in a separate AWS Region.
4.7.7. Testing the Recovered Maiora Fashion Store Website After the EC2 application server and RDS database have been restored and their configurations updated, the Maiora Fashion Store website is accessed for verification.
The following application functions are checked:
The website homepage loads successfully. Product information is displayed. Product images can be retrieved from Amazon S3. User login and registration pages are accessible. Shopping cart and order functions can be accessed. The verification confirms that the restored application components can work together and provide the main website functions.
4.7.8. Section Summary In this section, the recovery procedures for the EC2 application server and RDS database are demonstrated using available backup recovery points.
The Elastic IP address is reassociated when necessary, and replicated product images are checked in the Sydney Region.
The final website verification confirms whether the restored application infrastructure, database, and image storage can support the main functions of Maiora Fashion Store.

The following information is checked:
Instance state. Instance type. Public IPv4 address or Elastic IP address, if configured. VPC and subnet association. The application server should be in the Running state when the website is being tested.

This activity helps verify that backup data is available for future restoration operations.
4.8.6. Cleaning Up Unnecessary AWS Resources After completing the deployment and testing activities, unnecessary resources are reviewed to reduce AWS costs.
The cleanup process includes:
Stopping EC2 instances that are no longer required. Deleting temporary EC2 instances created during restoration tests, if they are no longer needed. Reviewing unused EBS volumes and snapshots before deleting them. Reviewing RDS instances and deleting temporary restored instances only after confirming that they are no longer needed. Reviewing unused Elastic IP addresses and releasing them when appropriate. Keeping required backup recovery points and S3 data according to the project’s retention requirements. Before deleting any resource, its role in the application and backup process must be checked to avoid accidental data loss or service interruption.

Hosting the Maiora Fashion Store website on Amazon EC2. Storing application data in Amazon RDS for MySQL. Storing product images in Amazon S3. Creating EC2 and RDS recovery points through AWS Backup.
